title: Average Translational Kinetic Energy of Gas Molecule
topicTitle: Average translational kinetic energy of gas molecule
notes: Kinetic theory relates pressure to molecular motion: pV=(1/3)Nm⟨c²⟩. Combining this with pV=NkBT gives (1/2)m⟨c²⟩=(3/2)kBT, the average translational kinetic energy per molecule.

At fixed absolute temperature, different ideal-gas molecules have equal mean translational kinetic energy. Their speeds differ because a lighter molecule needs greater speed to have the same kinetic energy.
Per mole, the mean translational kinetic energy is (3/2)RT. At 300 K this is about (3/2)(8.314)(300)=3.74 kJ mol⁻¹, or 6.21×10⁻²¹ J per molecule.
The result is for translation only. In a monatomic ideal gas it accounts for all classical internal energy; diatomic and polyatomic gases can also store energy in rotation and vibration.
The root-mean-square speed follows from the same result: vrms=√(3kBT/m)=√(3RT/M). Use molecular mass with kB or molar mass with R.

The average translational kinetic energy of one ideal-gas molecule is (3/2) k T. It depends on the temperature and not on the mass. A hydrogen molecule and an oxygen molecule at the same temperature have the same average translational energy, and the hydrogen molecule is faster.

specificConditions: **Equipartition Result:** The average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\langle KE_{trans} angle =  rac{3}{2} k_B T =  rac{3}{2}  rac{R}{N_A} T$. This comes from 3 translational degrees of freedom, each contributing $ rac{1}{2} k_B T$ via equipartition.

**Temperature Proportionality:** $\langle KE_{trans} angle \propto T$ — absolute temperature is a direct measure of average translational kinetic energy. This is why Kelvin scale is fundamental: at $T=0$, translational KE is zero (classically).

**Internal Energy of Monatomic Gas:** For a monatomic ideal gas, $U = N \langle KE_{trans} angle =  rac{3}{2} nRT$. The internal energy is purely translational KE. For diatomic/polyatomic gases, $U$ includes rotational and vibrational contributions as well.
